newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's bonuses anger some names -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's bonuses anger some names -- paper.

text.p: Some Lloyd's names are furious that company chairman David Rowland will get a 400,000 stg bonus as a reward for reforms credited with saving the company from collapse, the Times reported in its Monday edition.

It said the bonuses for Rowland and other senior executives would be announced in the next annual report. It quoted Christopher Stockwell, chairman of the Lloyd's Names Association Working Party, as saying they were out of line.
"The thousands of names who accepted the settlement offer under duress, in what was a fudged deal without honesty or credit, will find the bonuses totally unacceptable," he said.
"The bonus for Mr Rowland is in recognition of the central role he played in saving Lloyd's," the newspaper quoted a spokesman for the London association of underwriters as saying.
"He made a lot of personal sacrifices."

According to the newspaper, Rowland, who makes 500,000 stg a year, had refused pay rises or bonuses since he joined the company in 1993 until he thought the insurance market's problems had been solved.
